You will lead the development of an ambitious public affairs strategy, working closely with senior executives to ensure external engagement supports wider business priorities and long-term growth. ‍ Alongside leading a small team, you will play a key role in strengthening the organisation's external profile, building influential stakeholder relationships and identifying opportunities to shape policy conversations in a meaningful way. ‍ ‍ Main Responsibilities ‍ Develop and deliver a proactive public affairs strategy aligned to organisational and commercial objectives. Provide strategic counsel and brief senior executives on political and policy developments. Lead, coach and develop a small public affairs team, fostering a collaborative and high-performing culture. Build and maintain trusted relationships across Westminster, Whitehall, trade associations and other key external stakeholders. Manage external public affairs agencies, ensuring high-quality delivery and measurable outcomes. Monitor the evolving political landscape, identifying emerging risks and opportunities. Work collaboratively with colleagues across communications, marketing, brand and wider business functions to deliver integrated campaigns. Manage budgets and ensure public affairs activity demonstrates clear value and impact. ‍ ‍ Skills & Experience ‍ Significant experience leading public affairs within an in-house team, consultancy, trade association or comparable environment. Alongside recruitment, you'll help deliver our industry-leading events and thought leadership programme, including market insight reports, the Annual Political Cartoon Awards and the Communications Director's Network. ‍ You'll bring: ‍ Experience in public affairs, corporate affairs, communications or a related consultancy. Commercial awareness and an interest in executive search. Strong written communication and attention to detail.
